scope.summary: Establish the early canonical task-oriented Tailor UserManual framework, generated command/help bindings, BLOCKED-entry contract, and no-context discovery harness; MT-781 exclusively owns final content completeness and end-to-end manual-only operation proof, while legacy ModelManual content remains a compatibility shim only.
acceptance_criteria: The framework defines the chapter taxonomy for opening/navigating, project lifecycle, garment authoring, sewing/arrangement, simulation/repair, BodyKit, anatomy/contact, PoseKit/sheets, materials, animation, publishing/DCC, diagnostics/recovery, and parallel-agent operation; unavailable chapters/actions carry typed BLOCKED owner, dependency, and recovery fields and MUST NOT imply completeness.

For actions available at this stage, exact commands, inputs, outputs, permissions, preconditions, errors, receipts, recovery actions, stable control ids, and context-help links are generated from the canonical command/surface corpus; missing bindings fail the framework check rather than being filled by prose.

Early no-context tests prove manual discovery, generated binding consistency, BLOCKED navigation, and the currently available representative paths only; final chapter completeness plus backend-only and GUI-only end-to-end manual operation is accepted exclusively by MT-781 and cannot be claimed by this MT.
scope.risk_if_missed: Hundreds of MT-number pages would be unusable to operators and no-context models during real production or failure recovery.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Non-UI contract: typed commands, state, receipts, diagnostics, and TraceProjection provide model/operator observability; the owning native projection is separately contracted.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > Manual framework > Navigation, blocked entries, and generated command help

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: The early UserManual framework and consistency scan do not execute product actions; documented actions retain their own runtime events.
The framework check must emit typed missing-anchor, stale-binding, unresolved-BLOCKED-owner, and no-context discovery defects.
Manual generation and consistency checks have no application, device, or child-process watch surface.

risks: Hundreds of MT-number pages would be unusable to operators and no-context models during real production or failure recovery.
GUI, backend, agent, replay, and manual projections may drift if they do not consume the same typed authority.
minimum_controls: One typed owner and exact stable ids are required.
Negative, concurrent, cancellation, recovery, and no-context proofs are required where applicable.
No validator PASS/FAIL is inferred from this pre-activation contract.
